key_insight: DATPO shows that improving the structure of RLVR rollouts—not just reward optimization—can substantially expand reasoning coverage (pass@k) by encouraging diverse, tree-based exploration.
engineering_relevance: For mathematical reasoning systems, training-time rollout design can directly improve downstream test-time scaling by finding more correct reasoning paths, not just boosting single-answer accuracy.
method: Difficulty-adaptive tree search allocates exploration based on problem difficulty.
Sentence-entropy-guided forking increases semantic diversity and avoids token-level branching locality.
A sibling-diversity advantage term explicitly rewards diverse reasoning trajectories during policy optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks where DATPO outperforms baselines, especially in pass@k, indicating better reasoning coverage and scaling performance.
watch_item: The approach may add training complexity and sensitivity to how difficulty estimation and entropy-based branching are implemented.
paper_title: Difficulty-Adaptive Tree-Structured Policy Optimization for Expanding Reasoning Coverage in RLVR
